extracted.intended_audience: policy makers, national and regional IP offices, researchers, economists, IP professionals and data analysts
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, metrics and methodological guidance for measuring and reporting patent activity (applications, grants, families, in-force patents, technology breakdowns and related statistical concepts) used in WIPO's annual World Intellectual Property Indicators report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent applications (worldwide)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of patent applications filed worldwide in a given year (e.g., “Applicants around the world filed 3.2 million patent applications in 2019”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported totals may be driven by particular offices or resident filing behavior (example: decline in China drove 2019 fall). Long-term trends and year-on-year growth rates are provided; interpret annual changes in light of domestic policy/regulatory shifts and resident vs non-resident composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident versus non-resident applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident applications: filed at the IP office of the state/jurisdiction where the first named applicant resides. Non-resident applications: filed at an office in which the first named applicant is not domiciled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compute resident share of filings and to explain drivers of growth/decline. Example: resident share decreased from 71.5% in 2018 to 69.2% in 2019, mainly due to fall in resident filings in China.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin of application (country/region)
rubrics_metrics.description: For statistical purposes, the origin of an application means the country or territory of residence of the first named applicant in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: in some cases (notably the U.S.) origin may be determined by the assignee rather than the applicant. Origin-based statistics complement office-based (received) statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent application count
rubrics_metrics.description: Method to count applications at regional IP offices as equivalent to multiple national applications (used when reporting data by origin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For OAPI, EAPO, GCC Patent Office, each application is multiplied by the number of member states; for ARIPO and EPO, counting rules differ (see report). The equivalent application concept is used to avoid under-counting regionally-filed applications when reporting origin data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent families
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of interrelated patent applications filed at one or more offices to protect the same invention, linked by priority claim, PCT national phase entry, continuation, continuation-in-part, internal priority, addition or division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent family indicators are used to adjust for multiple filings of the same invention; foreign-oriented patent families are those with at least one filing office differing from the applicant’s origin. Family size (number of offices) indicates geographical coverage; most families are filed at a single office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign-oriented patent families
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent families that have at least one filing office which differs from the office of the applicant’s country of origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such families may still include only one filing office (e.g., a foreign applicant filing directly in a foreign office). Used to measure cross-border patenting and outward internationalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent applications filed abroad (filings abroad)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of equivalent or origin-based applications that applicants file in foreign offices (i.e., applications abroad).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to measure internationalization of applicants (e.g., U.S. applicants filed ~236,000 applications abroad in 2019). Compare filings abroad across origins and over time to assess globalization of patenting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of patents issued (granted) by patent offices in a given year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant counts are affected by examination capacity and procedural delays and therefore should not be directly compared with application counts in the same year. Interpret cross-office differences in grants with awareness of procedural and capacity differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents in force
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of patents that remain valid and enforceable in a jurisdiction at a point in time (i.e., not lapsed or expired).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents in force depend on maintenance/renewal fee payments; report includes totals by office, resident vs non-resident composition, average patent age, and proportion surviving at least seven years or the full 20-year term for jurisdictions that provide time-series in-force data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance / Renewal (keeps patent in force)
rubrics_metrics.description: Process by which protection of an IP right is maintained, usually by paying renewal fees at regular intervals; failure to pay may cause lapse before full term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to interpret patents-in-force and survival statistics (e.g., percent of patents remaining in force after 7 or 20 years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident patent applications per unit of GDP
rubrics_metrics.description: A normalized metric: resident patent applications per USD 100 billion of GDP (or similar GDP-normalized ratios).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare patenting intensity across economies of different sizes (e.g., Republic of Korea leads with 7,779 resident applications per USD 100bn GDP in 2019). Interpret with caution—economic structure and income group affect ratios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident patent applications per population
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident patent applications normalized per million population (or other per-capita measure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an alternative normalization to GDP; rankings may differ subtly from GDP-adjusted metrics. Useful alongside GDP-adjusted metrics to understand relative patenting activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent families (unique inventions) indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of patent families (unique inventions) as an indicator to avoid double-counting multiple filings for the same invention across jurisdictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to measure underlying inventive activity (e.g., families worldwide reached ~1.98 million in 2017). Family creation and family size statistics provide insight into geographic filing strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology-field classification (IPC-based field mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment of patent applications/publications to technology fields based on International Patent Classification (IPC) symbols mapped to technology categories (e.g., computer technology, electrical machinery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPC-to-field correspondence is not always clear-cut; mappings are likely to capture the majority but may miss edge cases. Report provides IPC symbol lists for several fields (and cautions about imperfect correspondence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication date (patent publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: The date on which a patent application is disclosed to the public; on that date the subject matter becomes prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication-year-based statistics have a lag (publication delay). Latest complete published-application data can trail the application year due to publication timelines; interpret technology-field statistics and publication-year series accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority date
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of the application on the basis of which priority is claimed (Paris Convention right of priority).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority date is used in family linkage and novelty assessments; it anchors comparisons across jurisdictions and in defining patent family creation dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: All information disclosed to the public about an invention, in any form, before a given date; used to determine novelty and inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant for international searches and preliminary examinations; informs patentability assessment procedures reported by offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application filed with a patent office for which no patent has yet been granted or refused and which has not been withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In jurisdictions requiring an examination request, pending may refer to applications for which a request has been received or those awaiting such request. Pending counts reflect backlogs and procedural regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent is a set of exclusive rights granted for inventions that are new, non-obvious (involve an inventive step) and industrially/commercially applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This legal standard underlies examination and grant decisions reported by offices; differences in how offices apply these standards and their examination capacity affect grants and rejections across jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT (Patent Cooperation Treaty) application and national phase
rubrics_metrics.description: A PCT application is an international application filed under the PCT; the national phase follows the international phase and consists of entry/processing in individual countries/regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCT-system filings and national-phase entries are used to measure international filing strategies; PCT-based family linkages feature in family indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT-PPH pilots (patent prosecution highway)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bilateral agreements between patent offices enabling applicants to request accelerated examination based on positive findings by an International Searching Authority or International Preliminary Examining Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPH pilots affect examination speed and grant statistics; consider their presence when comparing time-to-grant and grant volumes across offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: National route / Paris route / Hague and Madrid routes (filing routes)
rubrics_metrics.description: National (Paris) route: filing directly with national/regional offices. Hague: for industrial designs; Madrid: for trademarks; PCT: for patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different filing routes affect counting (office receipts vs origin data) and equivalence calculations; report distinguishes routes when analyzing filings by origin and office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model (petty/short-term patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: A special form of patent right with shorter term and often less-stringent patentability requirements, known also as petty patents, short-term patents or innovation patents in some countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility model application and grant counts are reported separately from patents; include when comparing inventive activity across jurisdictions that make heavy use of utility models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microorganism deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: The transmittal and storage of a microorganism with an International Depositary Authority (IDA), as part of disclosure requirements for certain biotechnological patent filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant to patents involving microorganisms; deposit details may be required for enabling disclosure and for national/regional examination procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent counts for trademarks (class counts) and industrial designs (design counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark statistics are based on equivalent trademark applications using class counts (number of classes specified). Industrial design statistics are based on design counts (number of designs in applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These equivalence concepts for other IP types are noted to clarify that WIPO uses analogous counting adjustments across IP categories; interpret totals accordingly when comparing across IP types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional application/grant counting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and rules for counting applications/grants filed at regional offices (ARIPO, OAPI, BOIP, EAPO, EPO, EUIPO, GCC Patent Office) when reporting origin or office statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional filings may be multiplied by member states for origin reporting or treated with special rules (e.g., ARIPO/EPO rules for resident vs abroad) — these affect equivalent-application counts and origin rankings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent examination outcome variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation that examination outcomes (grant vs refuse) vary greatly across offices due to differences in examination procedures, capacity and delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use caution comparing grant rates or counts across offices; differences may reflect procedural factors rather than differences in underlying patentability of inventions.
